environment: Queensland rooftops keep the solar crown as uptake climbs again this spring
Great Barrier Reef citizen scientists report encouraging coral recovery on inshore sites
science: Aussie researchers edge closer to cheaper, greener battery recycling tech
sports: NRL finals fever hits Queensland as the Broncos and Cowboys chase premiership glory
stories.overview: Humpback whale superhighway peaks off the south east coast as thousands cruise past on their spring migration

segments.title: The Open
segments.script: Gday and welcome to ParkSyde Bright Side, its Thursday the tenth of September and mate the coast is absolutely buzzing right now. Grab your morning cuppa because weve got whales, reefs, robots and finals footy all in one show today. Its officially spring in Queensland and honestly you can feel it, the mornings are crisp, the afternoons are golden and everyone is just that little bit happier. Im Jamie, hes Alex, and were here to remind you the news doesnt always have to be doom and gloom. Too right. Weve got a ripper overview story about our finned friends putting on a show off our coastline, plus some genuinely good news for the reef and the planet. Lets get into it.

segments.title: Green Desk
segments.script: Lets kick off green and gold, literally, because Queensland is once again leading the nation for rooftop solar. More households are clicking over to panels this spring, which means lower bills and a lighter footprint for the Sunshine State. Its funny, we complain about the heat up here but then we go and turn it into free power, thats peak Queensland problem solving right there. Meanwhile out on the reef, citizen scientists diving the inshore sites are reporting some genuinely encouraging coral recovery. Yeah after some tough bleaching years its lovely to hear divers talking about colour coming back rather than coral graveyards. Small wins, but they add up, and its proof that when locals get involved the reef actually has a fighting chance.

segments.title: Science & Tomorrow
segments.script: Righto, science corner, and this ones for anyone whos ever felt guilty chucking out a dead phone battery. Aussie researchers are making real headway on cheaper, greener ways to recycle old batteries instead of them ending up in landfill. Which matters more than ever with everyone driving electric cars and carrying about six devices in their bag at any given time. The idea is you pull the valuable metals back out and use them again instead of digging up more of the earth for them. Basically turning our tech rubbish bin into a bit of a gold mine, love that for us. Little breakthroughs like this dont always make the front page but theyre exactly the kind of quiet progress that adds up over time.

segments.title: Weather
segments.script: Cheers Alex, and good morning south east Queensland, Sam here with your spring outlook. Were looking at a cracker run of days ahead, plenty of sunshine, light coastal breezes and top temps sitting comfortably in the low to mid twenties across Brisbane, the Gold Coast and the Sunshine Coast. Overnight lows will still have a bit of a bite so dont pack away the doona just yet, but by afternoon its shorts and thongs weather for most of the region. Keep an eye out over the next week or so as spring storm season starts to wake up inland, but for today and the next few days its blue skies and barbecue conditions right along the coast. Back to you two.

segments.title: The Scoreboard
segments.script: Sport now and its finals time baby, the whole state has gone footy mad this week. The Broncos and the Cowboys are both deep in the NRL finals mix and youd want to have your jersey ironed and ready because September footy up here is basically a second religion. I love this time of year, the pubs are loud, the barbecues are firing and everyone suddenly becomes an expert on the wrestle in the ruck. Doesnt matter which team you follow, theres a genuine buzz across Queensland right now and thats good for everyone. Straight up finals footy plus spring weather is basically the Queensland dream combo. Get around your team this weekend, whoever they are, because this is the fun part of the season.

segments.title: Overview & Outro
segments.script: Right, before we go we promised you an awe inspiring one and here it is. Right now off our very own coastline, humpback whales are hitting the peak of their spring migration, with thousands cruising past on their way back down south. Honestly it still gives me goosebumps, these massive gentle giants breaching just offshore while were all going about our normal Tuesday, well today its Thursday but you get me. Whale watching boats out of the Gold Coast and Sunshine Coast are having an absolute ball this week. Its a proper reminder that this state of ours is a bit special, solar on the roofs, coral coming back on the reef and whales putting on a free show just past the breakers. Not bad for a Thursday. Not bad at all. Thats it for todays Bright Side, thanks for spending part of your morning with us. Get outside, look after each other, and well catch you same time tomorrow. Cheers Queensland.
